Chapter 7: A New World—University and the Challenge of Belonging
Imagine stepping off the bus and into a city that feels like a whole new universe. The noise, the crush of people, the energy that never seems to rest—it’s overwhelming, but there’s this spark of excitement running through it all. The university campus stretches out before him, buzzing with students from every corner of the country. For the boy, it’s a place filled with possibility, but also a swirl of uncertainty. Here, it’s no longer about his family’s past—now, it’s his own actions and choices that matter. Those first days? They blur together. New faces everywhere, customs that feel just a little out of reach, and a constant hum of ambition in the air. He can’t help but feel out of place among classmates who wear confidence like a second skin. Their clothes are sharper, their accents polished, their stories sparkling with experiences he’s only ever dreamed of. He’s painfully aware of his rough hands, the simplicity of his belongings—little traces of the village life that still cling to him.
But there’s something else, too—a sense of freedom he’s never known before. For the first time, he can speak up without fear, ask questions without worrying about having the “right” answer. Professors encourage debate, curiosity, and thinking for yourself. So, he dives into his studies, determined to prove he belongs. Long hours disappear in the library as he soaks up every bit of knowledge, pushing himself to keep up with the rest.
Of course, there are lonely moments—times when the distance from home feels like a mountain he’ll never cross. He misses his family, the comfort of village life, the sense that he truly belongs somewhere. Letters from home become tiny treasures, read and reread until the paper softens at the edges. When he writes back, he’s careful to hide the tough moments, wanting only to reassure his parents that all their sacrifices were worth it.
Slowly, things start to shift. He finds friends—other students who know what it’s like to feel out of place, who come from humble beginnings just like him. They trade stories, share laughter, and gather around late-night bowls of instant noodles. Together, they face university’s challenges, lean on each other during setbacks, and celebrate every small win.
The boy starts to explore new interests and fresh ways of thinking. He joins clubs, attends lectures, and lets himself imagine a future that once seemed out of reach. The city, with all its chaos and opportunities, feels less intimidating now. He learns how to carve out his own space, how to move through it all with a bit more confidence.
Still, the past isn’t something you just leave behind. He carries the lessons of the village wherever he goes—the value of hard work, the importance of family, the resilience that only comes from facing hardship. These are the things that set him apart, that give him strength when it all feels too much.
And as the years roll by, that boy grows into a young man, shaped by where he’s come from and where he’s headed. The journey? It’s never easy, but it’s his. In the end, he learns that belonging isn’t about trying to fit in—it’s about being true to who you are, no matter where you find yourself.
